version_rules: A DOI version of record uses its DOI plus publisher version or publication date.
An arXiv source uses the version-qualified arXiv identifier.
A repository source uses repository URL, commit SHA, and repository-relative path.
Same-work versions remain one source group and may not occupy separate folds.
A byte-identical digest or identical stable-source/version pair is a duplicate.

search_questions: Does a primary source support a typed directed relation from the proposed source object to the bridge object?
Does a primary source support a typed directed relation from the bridge object to the proposed target object?
Do exact passages establish compatible direction and polarity on both sides without relying on shared terminology alone?
Does direct A-to-C prior art, counterevidence, or a stated limitation defeat novelty or compatibility?
bridge_eligibility_conditions: Both relation sides bind exact source/version identities and exact passage locations.
Source object, bridge object, and target object types are declared and compatible.
Direction and polarity are explicit for both relations and are not inferred from topic overlap.
Assumptions and limitations are closed for each relation.
Direct A-to-C prior art and counterevidence searches are recorded under the same cutoff and budget.
Repeated historical pairs, renamed bridges, and unsupported abstract-only claims are ineligible.
positive_verdict_conditions: Both typed relation sides satisfy every eligibility condition.
Retained source bytes permit exact passage replay; unavailable bytes prohibit a positive verdict.
Direct A-to-C prior art and counterevidence records are complete and do not defeat the bridge claim.
The typed predication path is supported while both negative controls remain unsupported under equal budgets.
An independent reviewer confirms identity, relation compatibility, passages, controls, and limitations.
Positive technical review does not constitute human acceptance or runtime authorization.
stop_conditions: Stop and report unavailable when source identity, version, bytes, or exact passage location cannot be replayed.
Stop and reject on duplicate or historically repeated pair identity, reversed relation, incompatible object type, direction, or polarity.
Stop discovery at the frozen query and staged-import envelope.
Stop positive adjudication when direct prior art, counterevidence, or either negative control is unresolved.

eligibility_conditions: The finance source is genuine, independently inspectable, and bound to approved source bytes.
All registered coordinates, validation_target label, primary metric, and provenance are declared before splitting.
Two independent adjudications agree and a separate human corpus approval is digest-bound.
The source group is independent of every other eligible source group.
exclusion_conditions: Exclude abstract-only evidence, inferred coordinates, missing primary metric, missing provenance, or missing approval.
Exclude reviewer disagreement and changed source digest until resolved by a new adjudication.
Exclude duplicate versions as independent groups; DATA-NSQD-03 and DATA-NSQD-04 receive no automatic finance credit.

metrics.name: held_out_gain
metrics.definition: Arithmetic mean across five held-out folds of candidate occupied-cell count minus current-axis occupied-cell count, using identical held-out source groups.
metrics.unavailable_when: Fewer than five eligible source groups or any track lacks an identical fold population.

metrics.name: density
metrics.definition: For each held-out fold and track, eligible held-out record count divided by occupied held-out cell count; report the five fold values and arithmetic mean.
metrics.unavailable_when: The occupied held-out cell count is zero.

metrics.name: quality_weighted_diversity
metrics.definition: For each fold, sum the pre-split blinded quality weights represented by distinct occupied cells divided by total held-out quality weight; report fold values and arithmetic mean.
metrics.unavailable_when: Any held-out record lacks a pre-split blinded quality weight or total held-out quality weight is zero.

metrics.name: stability
metrics.definition: One minus population standard deviation of the five foldwise candidate-minus-current held-out gains divided by one plus the absolute arithmetic mean gain.
metrics.unavailable_when: Any of the five foldwise gains is unavailable or nonfinite.

metrics.name: redundancy
metrics.definition: Maximum bias-corrected Cramer's V between validation_target and each registered axis, fitted on training groups and evaluated on the corresponding held-out group; report all fold maxima and their arithmetic mean.
metrics.unavailable_when: A contingency table is degenerate or a held-out category was absent from its training groups.

metrics.name: residual_variation
metrics.definition: Held-out normalized conditional entropy H(validation_target given registered axes) divided by H(validation_target), with category support learned only from training groups; report fold values and arithmetic mean.
metrics.unavailable_when: Held-out validation_target entropy is zero or required category support is absent from training groups.

metrics.name: confound_sensitivity
metrics.definition: Maximum absolute difference between aggregate held-out gain and gain recomputed within each predeclared provenance-supported confound stratum, using unchanged folds and tracks.
metrics.unavailable_when: No confound strata were predeclared or any declared stratum lacks an eligible held-out observation.

metrics.name: interpretability
metrics.definition: Arithmetic mean of predeclared binary operationalizability ratings from independent reviewers blinded to track outcomes and source identity; retain each rating and disagreement.
metrics.unavailable_when: Reviewer independence, blinding, or a predeclared rating item is missing.

positive_selection_conditions: All eight metrics are replayable and finite or explicitly unavailable without imputation.
Candidate, current-axis, and shuffled-label tracks use identical eligible identities and folds.
A digest-bound human threshold decision predates decision-bearing outcome unblinding.
The smallest implementation wins every approved comparison required by that decision; otherwise retain the baseline or report no selection.
Any favorable result remains evaluation-only and does not admit validation_target or authorize runtime.
stop_conditions: Stop as unavailable below five eligible independent source groups.
Stop on duplicate versions across folds, inconsistent populations, missing provenance, nonfinite values, or imputation.
Stop decision-bearing interpretation until numeric thresholds receive explicit human approval before outcome unblinding.
Stop and reject any schema-admission or runtime-authority claim.

changed_condition_requirements: Each trigger names a measurable changed variable, original value, candidate value, comparison rule, and evidence digests.
A trigger is evaluated only against immutable evidence from the registered experiment.
Similarity alone, inferred improvement, or a missing failure is not a changed condition.
restart_condition_requirements: Each restart condition names a measurable predicate, required evidence digest, allowed scope, and independent decision owner.
Record admission, packet inclusion, resurrection, restart, and runtime authorization remain separate decisions.
No restart condition may infer satisfaction from similarity or from the record's own approval fields.
stop_conditions: Stop intake when any registered-experiment field, immutable evidence byte, digest, UTC execution time, measured outcome, changed condition, or restart condition is missing.
Stop and reject forbidden candidate classes, self-approval, stale digests, inferred restart, and record-field authority claims.
Stop before a new experiment unless its scientific purpose and full authorization request receive explicit human authorization.
Stop conditional ablations until a real independently approved record exists; successful or inconclusive experiments may leave G blocked.

global_stop_conditions: Stop if any acquisition outcome was observed before this protocol and manifest were frozen.
Stop on unexplained mutation of the successor baseline index, historical packet bytes, current C/F/G packet digests, or protected .playwright-mcp bytes.
Stop when the discovery envelope is exhausted; widening requires a new explicit human authorization before further acquisition.
Stop on missing or duplicate source/version identity, unresolved access authorization, or unrecorded retention state.
Stop on reviewer-producer identity or session conflict, self-approval, or technical review presented as human acceptance.
Stop decision use of thresholds chosen after outcomes, and retain all negative, null, unavailable, and counterevidence results.
Stop any product schema, CLI, configuration, admission, resurrection, restart, or runtime authority change under this protocol.
